title: The Reassured Soul and the Path of Hardship

paragraphs.text: The scene of the Day of Judgment continues. Your Lord will come, and the angels will come with Him, standing rank upon rank. Hell will be brought close, so that it can be seen. On that Day, man will finally remember, but his remembering will not help him at all. He will say, "I wish I had sent ahead some good for my life." He will realize too late what he should have prepared while he still had time. On that Day, no one will punish as Allah punishes, and no one will bind as He binds. Then the tone changes completely. To the righteous it will be said: "O soul that is at peace, return to your Lord, well pleased and pleasing to Him. Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise." These beautiful words end the surah with a picture of complete peace and acceptance, offering hope to everyone who strives to please Allah.

A new surah begins with an oath. Allah swears by this city, Makkah, while the Prophet is free of restriction in it. He also swears by a father and the one who is born of him. These oaths lead to a clear statement about human life: man has been created to face hardship and struggle. Life is not meant to be completely easy. Every person will meet difficulties, and how he responds to them is part of his test.

Next, the ayahs describe the attitude of a proud person. Does he think that no one will ever have power over him? He boasts, saying that he has spent a great deal of wealth. Does he think that no one has seen him? These questions show how foolish his pride is. Allah has always been aware of him and of everything he does. Then a question reminds him of Allah's gifts: did We not give him two eyes? With these eyes he can see the world, and he should also be able to see the truth. The ayahs remind the reader that every ability a person has is a gift, and that it should lead him to gratitude rather than pride.
